task: Turn the esl-likes Restaurant into a rush-hour service shift: replacement customers, a pure tested service director (warm-up / rush / final push) driven only by the service clock, overlapping demands, walk-in/walk-out, stronger bell and phase cues, and speech-focus audio ducking — without changing the English or regressing anything already validated.
notes: READ FIRST: SPEC.md §3 'Protected speech focus', SPEC.md §4 (especially 'Difficulty' and the new 'Service shift (revised 2026-09-13)'), and the last DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entries, especially '2026-09-13 — Rush-hour revision'. Those are the frozen contract; where this brief and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins — say so in your summary.

STABLE BASE — DO NOT REGRESS (all validated on the committed build): 3/4/5 tables with live-order limits 1/3/4 where a raised hand counts against the limit; whole-room fixed camera; foods independent with repeats, delivery matched by FOOD not plate; wrong delivery = Japanese refusal, English not repeated, dish stays in hand, refusal lock, step-away, first-try and combo lost; a raised hand can be answered while carrying (it takes the order, never counts as a wrong delivery); click-to-walk steers around tables (autoWalkAim); targetQuestion refuses to open a prompt for anyone but the click-to-walk target; questionCustomerStillNear keeps an open prompt; speechFocus service clock freezes all pressure; Listen Again forfeits only the memory bonus; turnaround; finish() payload; full disposal in exit().
WHY: the game still feels like one small errand after another. The goal is 'I am running a busy dining room and several things need me at once' — more simultaneous demands, not harder English.

SHIFT STRUCTURE (frozen numbers): Easy 3 tables / limit 1 / 5 customers total; Normal 4 tables / limit 3 / 7 total; Challenge 5 tables / limit 4 / 8 total. The shift ends when every customer in the total is resolved (delivered or left) — keep updateRoundEnd semantics on the TOTAL, not on the seated set. Start with tables filling over the first few seconds (staggered, not all on frame 0). When a customer is served they eat briefly (a few seconds, dish stays on their table) then walk out; when a customer's patience runs out they walk out as today. Either way the table frees, and after a short randomised delay (director-controlled) a NEW customer walks in from the open front of the room to that chair with a NEW independently random food (pickFood). A table must never predict a food. Stop seating once the total has been handed out; the room may thin only at the very end.

DATA MODEL: today customers and dishes are pre-created 1:1 by index with index === table. Replacements break that. Give each customer its own id/index (0..total-1) and a table reference; create the dish with the customer (or on order), keep delivery matched by food among awaiting customers; make sure leaveCustomer's dish discard, records, refusal locks and the debug snapshot all key off the customer, never the table. CUSTOMER_MODELS/TINTS have 5 looks for up to 8 customers: vary model+tint combinations so consecutive occupants of the same table look different, and customers in the room at the same time are distinguishable. Reuse/dispose character instances correctly — no leaks across a shift.

SERVICE DIRECTOR: create src/minigames/restaurant/director.js, a PURE module (no DOM, no three.js) with an injectable rng, advanced only with service time, e.g. createRestaurantDirector({ level, tables, total, rng }) exposing advance(serviceDt, view) -> list of events such as { type: 'seat', table }, { type: 'raiseHand', customer }, plus phase ('warmup' | 'rush' | 'finalPush') and progress. The controller owns scene state and passes a small view (per-table occupancy, per-customer state, live orders, focusReleasedAgo). Keep dish preparation time a property of the food (FOOD_PREP_SECONDS × prepScale) but let the director SPACE ready events so two dishes never become ready in the same frame (at least ~0.8–1.0 s of service time apart, by briefly delaying the later one). Director rules: warm-up ≈ first 18 s of service time, at most 2 simultaneous demands and gentler delays; rush = normal delays; final push starts once the last customer of the total has been seated (shorter replacement and settle delays, small cue). A newly seated customer settles 1–2.5 s (randomised) before raising a hand; never raise several hands on the same frame; after speech focus ends hold NEW discrete events (seat, raise hand, ready) for ~0.8 s of service time so the child is not ambushed, but never hold patience. Idle guard: in the rush on Normal/Challenge, if live orders + raised hands is below 2 and a table is free or a seated customer is settling, shorten the next delay so the room does not go serial or empty. Easy stays calm and never exceeds one live order.

The director must read only the service clock: speech focus (focus.serviceDelta) freezes seating, hand raising, readiness, walking in/out, eating and replacement delays by construction. Do not add per-timer focus guards.

FEEL: (1) bell: louder and unmistakable — a quick two-tone ding (two playSfx calls, gain ~0.2) plus the existing ring cue; with several ready dishes the counter must stay readable. (2) Raised hand: keep the ❓ cue and emote; add a quick pop sfx when a hand goes up. (3) Customers visibly walk in to their chair and walk out (service-time driven, short, ≤ ~1.5 s each way), no clipping through tables — reuse the steering idea. (4) Phase cues: a small top-centre pill using UI.restaurant.rush when the rush starts (after warm-up) and UI.restaurant.finalPush at the final push — small, brief, never covering customers or the counter. (5) A small progress counter in the scene card or corner using formatUi(UI.restaurant.progress, { done, total }) where done = resolved customers. (6) Combo pop as today. (7) Call audio.setFocusDuck(true) whenever focus begins and audio.setFocusDuck(false) when it ends and in exit() (audio.setFocusDuck exists in src/systems/audio.js; do not modify audio.js). REJECTED, do not add: footstep sounds, continuous ambience, a two-dish tray, any countdown timer.
STRINGS: UI.restaurant.rush, UI.restaurant.finalPush and UI.restaurant.progress already exist in src/config/lesson.js. Do not edit lesson.js.

DWELL TO TALK (SPEC §3 'Dwell to talk'; the shared foundation is already built — src/systems/talkDwell.js, src/config/interaction.js, speech.listenOnce() and speech.autoListenAllowed(); read them, do not modify them). Replace proximity-opens-prompt with the dwell: each frame, with REAL frame dt (service keeps running during a dwell), call dwell.update(dt, { candidates: customers in state 'orderCue' as { id, x, z, radiusSq: CUSTOMER_RADIUS_SQ }, player: { x, z, forwardX: Math.sin(player.rotation.y), forwardZ: Math.cos(player.rotation.y) } (Kenney models face +z), moving: movement input non-zero OR an auto-walk in progress, lockedTargetId: the click-to-walk customer's id or null }). While dwelling or ready: draw a simple progress ring on that customer (lightweight, reuse the billboard approach, never food-related) and turn them slightly toward the player (clamped yaw, restored after); show the HUD talk control via promptQuestion WITHOUT speech focus so a manual hold works. Commit when phase becomes 'ready', or at once when a manual hold starts (speech state LISTENING), or — in mic-free mode — when ready: call dwell.commit(), focus.begin(), audio.setFocusDuck(true), play a soft ready chime, and in mic mode call speech.listenOnce() only when speech.autoListenAllowed() (otherwise leave the hold control waiting); in mic-free mode show the existing fallback at commit. On acceptance call dwell.notifyAccepted(id); on a failed attempt (speech TRY_AGAIN) or walking away call dwell.notifyEnded(id, 'failed' | 'cancelled') so nothing auto-reopens while the child stands still; manual hold remains available. On click-to-walk arrival rotate the avatar to face the clicked customer so the dwell starts without another click; while walking, never dwell on or prompt anyone but the click target (keep the existing targetQuestion guard). Delivery, collecting and Listen Again keep their explicit controls. When AUTO_TALK_ENABLED is false keep today's proximity-opens-prompt behaviour. The camera does NOT move. The playthrough must now stop and face (click the customer and wait for the dwell) before the fallback appears; prove the scripts/lib/mockSpeech.mjs mock with one mic-mode check (a scripted correct question is accepted after the dwell; scripted silence ends in try-again and the mic does not reopen while standing still — assert the mock's start counter) in addition to the mic-free sessions, and check that running past a raised hand without stopping opens no prompt.

KEEP ENGLISH CENTRAL: no order tickets, no food icons over customers, no highlighting of the right table while carrying, no arrows. Difficulty comes from workload only; never touch recognition windows, fallback, or retry policy.

SCORING: scoreSession(records) stays pure and unchanged in spirit; with more customers it simply receives more records. Ensure every customer in the total produces exactly one record (delivered or left).

DEBUG HOOK: extend window.__eslDebug.restaurant with phase, progress { done, total }, per-customer id/index and table, each customer's state including seating/walking/eating/leaving states, and keep existing fields (customers[].index/state/food/cueShowing/screen/patience/refusalRemaining, readyDishes, carried, combo, focusActive, activeOrderLimit, player). Screen positions must be correct for walking customers.

UNIT TESTS: src/minigames/restaurant/director.test.mjs (node:test + node:assert/strict, seeded rng) covering at least: replacement seating after a table frees; replacement foods independent with repeats possible (via pickFood through an injected rng); total respected and the shift resolves; Easy never exceeds one live order; Normal reaches 3 and Challenge 4 live orders under a simulated attentive player; ready events never share a frame; advance(0) produces no events (speech focus freezes the director); no new discrete events within the post-focus hold; hands do not all rise on the same frame; the idle guard prevents long empty stretches in the rush; phases progress warm-up → rush → final push.

PLAYTHROUGH: update scripts/playthrough.mjs (level 2) for the shift — the session loop must keep interleaving asking and delivering until the whole TOTAL is resolved, handle replacement customers appearing at freed tables, and keep both sessions (listening → three stars; anti-shortcut sweep → finishes, not three stars) and all existing checks. Add checks: a replacement customer is seated after someone leaves; the shift total is reported and reached; phase reaches rush. FIX A KNOWN FLAKE in the anti-shortcut sweep: today it forces a wrong first offer only when a wrong-food, non-cue customer happens to be offerable, so when random foods and resolved tables leave only the right customer it delivers first try by elimination and can legitimately reach three stars (observed 2026-09-13: one refusal, 3/4 first-try, 3 stars, check failed). Make the sweep deterministic: never deliver a plate first try while the shift can still produce a wrong target — hold the dish (or collect another) and wait until an unresolved customer with a different food is offerable, which replacement customers make possible; only the final unavoidable plates may go first try. Read the resulting records' first-try share from the debug hook or the saved result and assert that it is below the first-try cap in src/minigames/restaurant/scoring.js AND that stars < 3, so the check asserts the scoring rule rather than hoping the foods cooperate. HARNESS PITFALLS from this project: after an accepted mic-free answer the fallback buttons stay visible ~0.6 s — wait for them to clear before approaching the next customer; detect outcomes from debug-state transitions, never leftover bubble text; never assert a quantity reached after a fixed-duration wait under software GL, loop until the state is reached; never crash on a missing answer — record a FAIL with screenshot and debug state and continue or break cleanly.

BEHAVIOURAL ACCEPTANCE is owned by the controller: your sandbox cannot start the preview server, so do not burn time trying to run npm run playthrough. Make sure npm test and npm run build pass, and syntax-check the playthrough with node --check. Report behavioralValidation honestly (observed: false). Claude will run the playthrough, probes and a visual pass.

Append a short DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entry only for decisions this brief and SPEC do not cover (for example eating time or the look-variation rule). Do not rewrite existing entries and do not edit SPEC.md.
requirements: Easy/Normal/Challenge use 3/4/5 tables, live-order limits 1/3/4, and shift totals 5/7/8; the round ends only when every customer in the total is delivered or has left
Freed tables are re-seated after a director-controlled randomised delay by new customers who walk in, with independently random foods (repeats allowed); tables never predict food
Served customers eat briefly then walk out; customers whose patience runs out walk out; both free the table

src/minigames/restaurant/director.js is pure (no DOM/three.js), rng-injectable, advanced only by service time, and produces warm-up → rush → final push phases with staggered hands, spaced ready events and a post-focus event hold
Normal and Challenge regularly overlap a raised hand, cooking, a ready dish and a known unresolved order; Easy never exceeds one live order
All pressure — seating, hands, readiness, walking, eating, replacement delays, patience, cooling, refusal locks — freezes while speech focus is active

audio.setFocusDuck is set on focus begin/end and cleared in exit; the bell is a louder two-tone ding; a hand-raise pop plays; rush and final-push cues are small pills; a small progress counter shows done/total
Customer data, dishes, records, refusal locks and the debug snapshot are keyed by customer, not table, and characters are created and disposed without leaks across the shift
No order tickets, food icons, table highlighting, arrows, countdowns, footsteps, ambience or two-dish tray are added
Every validated behaviour listed under STABLE BASE still works
src/minigames/restaurant/director.test.mjs covers the listed cases and passes; npm test passes including all pre-existing tests; npm run build is clean
scripts/playthrough.mjs drives the full shift with both sessions and the added checks, avoids the listed harness pitfalls, and passes node --check

Asking uses dwell to talk per SPEC §3: no prompt or focus while passing by; dwell locks its customer; commit starts focus, ducks audio, chimes and auto-listens only when allowed; mic-free opens the fallback after the dwell; manual hold bypasses the dwell; failed or cancelled attempts never auto-reopen while standing still; click-to-walk arrival faces and dwells; the camera does not move
The playthrough proves the speech mock (accepted after dwell; silence does not reopen the mic) and checks that running past a raised hand opens no prompt
